findings.evidence: The Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model, developed by the Center for Creative Leadership, provides a structured approach to giving clear, objective feedback that minimizes defensiveness and promotes improvement.
findings.fix: Delete the model exposition and 'Why SBI Works' tutorial; keep only the worked examples and calibration notes the model would not produce on its own
Trim the phrase banks ('You always...' -> 'I've noticed a pattern...') to the few substitutions that fix non-obvious failures; the model generates the rest unprompted
Cut the RACI table and vague/explicit pairs (standard PM content) down to the trade-off framing and scope-change template this skill actually routes to
Add the non-obvious ordering decisions (when to skip steps, which evidence to gather before drafting, when one example beats dated history) instead of the generic prepare-deliver-agree-follow-up arc
Add 1-2 environment-specific traps with consequences (e.g., HR processes that require contemporaneous documentation, channels with retention/legal discovery)

findings.evidence: Preserve only information appropriate to the user's role and workplace policy.
findings.fix: Give a concrete test for 'appropriate' (role need-to-know, policy check, ask the user when in doubt) so the confidentiality rule is decidable

findings.evidence: Uses Situation-Behavior-Impact or equivalent observable-fact framing
findings.fix: Drop 'or equivalent' and require situation, behavior, and impact to be separately identifiable so the assertion is verifiable

findings.evidence: agree on a specific next step and check-in
findings.fix: State a default check-in cadence and a one-line summary template for step 4 so follow-up is actionable without guessing
